Roblox claims it has made changes to its hugely popular children's app to protect kids from bad actors, but regulators say these protections are not enough.

The regulator identified four significant shortcomings, including the ability for adults to send friend requests to children without parental approval……

Australia's eSafety Commissioner today outlined the vulnerabilities found during testing:

  • Adults can send friend requests to young Australian children without parental or guardian consent;
  • Children and adults can view and respond to each other's posts on forums outside the game environment without parental or guardian consent;
  • Children's friendships are visible to anyone on the Roblox platform;
  • Children's personal information and profiles, including account names, the number and names of friends, avatar images, and non-sensitive personal information such as interests, are visible to anyone on the Roblox platform, and there is no way to limit who can see this information

The regulator said Roblox has agreed to implement stricter measures within three months:

  • Prevent adults from contacting children they do not know without parental consent
  • Strengthen children's account settings so they are private by default
  • Provide easy-to-use reporting mechanisms and notify users of the outcome of complaints
  • Engage an independent third-party auditor to review the effectiveness of its safety measures, including the deployment of age estimation measures

Roblox has more than 380 million active users, the majority of whom are under the age of 16.
